evals.prompt: Deep study on Daniel 8:13-14. Want word studies on the key Hebrew terms, EGW references, SDABC insights, and how this connects to the sanctuary doctrine.
evals.expected_output: Full 8-section study in markdown, Standard or Exhaustive depth, closing with a Verification Ledger. Key Hebrew terms studied: e.g. 'erev boqer' (evening-morning, 2300), 'nitsdaq' (cleansed/restored). Andrews Bible Commentary and SDABC both attempted via egw-fetch.sh and reported honestly. EGW from Great Controversy on the sanctuary and judgment, fetched with para_id. Doukhan or Davidson cited as Adventist scholars on sanctuary, with pointers distinguished from claims. Cross-references include Lev 16, Heb 8-10, Rev 11:19. Theological themes connect explicitly to Adventist sanctuary doctrine, and at least one theme traces the passage to Christ.
expectations: Output contains all 8 sections in order: Passage Context, Historical Background, Word Studies, Commentary Insights, EGW Cross-References, Scriptural Cross-References, Theological Themes, Application Questions
Section 1 includes a literary-shape note on how the chapter's vision-plus-audition structure is built
Word studies include 3-5 words with Hebrew/transliteration, KJV and TB translation comparison
Word studies cover 'nitsdaq' (cleansed/justified/restored) — the disputed term in Dan 8:14
Strong's numbers appear only where certain; no approximated numbers
Commentary section references Andrews Bible Commentary by name, with access attempted and the outcome reported honestly
Commentary section references SDABC on the year-day principle and 1844 chronology
Commentary section names at least one Adventist scholar by specialty: Doukhan, Davidson, Goldstein, or Holbrook
Commentary section includes at least one classic non-Adventist voice with any doctrinal disagreement flagged
EGW section cites specific works with page numbers and para_id where fetched, OR clearly paraphrases without quote marks — no fabricated verbatim quotes
Cross-references include connection-type tags in table format
Theological themes engage the Adventist sanctuary doctrine explicitly, and at least one theme traces the passage to Christ
Application questions are 5-8, not all yes/no answerable
Document closes with a Verification Ledger table carrying a provenance tag for every source claim
No provenance tags, no para_id, no 'this session', and no first-person research narration in the body of the study

evals.prompt: Study Mark 2:23-28. I want to understand the original cultural context, what the Pharisees were actually objecting to, and how Jesus's response shapes Adventist Sabbath theology.
evals.expected_output: Full 8-section study. Historical background details first-century Pharisaic halakhah on Sabbath (39 categories, Mishnah tractate Shabbat). Word studies on Sabbath, Son of Man, Lord. Tonstad or Bacchiocchi cited for Sabbath theology. Matthew Henry and Keener used for cultural context, with the Sabbath-abrogation divergence flagged. EGW from Desire of Ages on the Sabbath conflicts. Themes connect Jesus's lordship over the Sabbath to the SDA position that Sabbath is for humanity and is not abolished.
expectations: Output contains all 8 sections in order, plus a Verification Ledger
Historical background explains Pharisaic Sabbath halakhah with specifics (39 categories of work, Mishnah references)
Word studies include 'Sabbath' and at least one of 'Son of Man' (huios tou anthropou) or 'Lord' (kurios)
Commentary section references Andrews Bible Commentary and SDABC on Mark 2
Commentary section names at least one Adventist Sabbath scholar: Tonstad, Bacchiocchi, or MacCarty
Calvin or another classic voice on Sabbath abrogation is flagged explicitly as diverging from the Adventist position
EGW section references Desire of Ages on Mark 2 / Sabbath conflicts with proper citation or labeled paraphrase
Theological themes engage the Adventist Sabbath doctrine — Sabbath for humanity, Christ as Lord of the Sabbath, not abolished — and one theme traces the passage to Christ
Cross-references include Gen 2:1-3, Ex 20, and at least two NT parallels
Application questions are 5-8, with at least one observational, one interpretive, and several applicational

evals.prompt: Romans 8:1-11. Word studies on 'condemnation,' 'flesh,' and 'Spirit.' Cross-references, Ellen White connections, and theological themes for an Adventist congregation.
evals.expected_output: Full 8-section study. Word studies on katakrima, sarx, pneuma with KJV and TB comparison. Heppenstall or LaRondelle cited for salvation theology. Matthew Henry on Romans 8 included, devotional application noted, soul-immortality assumptions flagged only where relevant. EGW from Steps to Christ / Selected Messages on righteousness by faith. Themes: no condemnation, life in the Spirit, sanctification flowing from justification. Romans 8 is NOT forced into a sanctuary or Sabbath reading.
expectations: Output contains all 8 sections in order, plus a Verification Ledger
Word studies include katakrima, sarx, pneuma with Greek transliteration and translation comparison
Translation comparison includes KJV and at least one other version
A lexicon is named where a word study leans on one (BDAG, Thayer's, BDB, HALOT)
Commentary section references Andrews Bible Commentary and SDABC on Romans 8
Commentary section names at least one Adventist salvation scholar: Heppenstall, LaRondelle, Knight, or Whidden
Commentary section includes Matthew Henry on Romans 8, fetched verbatim where possible
EGW section references appropriate works with proper citation or labeled paraphrase — no fabricated verbatim quotes
Cross-references include Gal 5:16-25, Ezek 36:26-27, John 3:5-8
Theological themes engage justification AND sanctification, noting the Adventist righteousness-by-faith emphasis
Theological themes are honest — Romans 8 is not forced into a sanctuary or Sabbath reading
Application questions are 5-8, with concrete cost in the applicational ones

evals.prompt: Do a deep study on 1 Corinthians 14 for a class that will ask about modern speaking in tongues. I want to know what BRI actually says.
evals.expected_output: Full study whose BRI section reports the real BRI position from the actual articles, retrieved with scripts/bri-fetch.py despite the live site's 403. BRI holds that tongues in Scripture are Spirit-given real human languages, not ecstatic utterance, and that modern glossolalia should not be equated with the NT gift. Ledger records the Wayback snapshot dates. Tests the anti-fabrication path end to end: the skill must not report BRI as unreadable, and must not invent its position either.
expectations: The BRI section reports actual article content, not a list of links the skill could not open
bri-fetch.py (or the documented manual Wayback + __NEXT_DATA__ fallback) is used after the live site returns 403
BRI's position is stated accurately: tongues as real human languages, not ecstatic speech; modern glossolalia not equated with the NT gift
Article titles and publication years are given, and the Wayback snapshot date is recorded in the ledger
Ledger marks the retrieved BRI articles fetched-verbatim, and any inaccessible page located-unread with the reason
No fabricated BRI content, and no claim that BRI is inaccessible when the fetcher works
Gerhard Hasel's Speaking in Tongues is surfaced as the fuller Adventist treatment if the BRI footnotes name it
The body contains no provenance tags, no HTTP codes, and no first-person account of what was or was not retrieved

No contents block needed at this length. The skill must not deliver a 6,000-word study when overview was requested.
expectations: Total body length is close to 1,200 words, and clearly not a full Standard-depth study

Roughly 2 word studies rather than 3-5
Roughly 3 cross-references and 3 application questions
Commentary tiers are each covered in about a paragraph

evals.prompt: Study Mark 16:9-20 on the great commission and the signs that follow believers.
evals.expected_output: A study that flags the textual variant honestly and early. Mark 16:9-20 is absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the KJV includes it because the Textus Receptus does. The study should say which witnesses support what, avoid building doctrine on the disputed ending without noting the dispute, and still treat the passage pastorally rather than dismissing it.
expectations: Section 1 flags the textual variant, naming the major witnesses that omit the long ending
The KJV's inclusion is explained as following the Textus Receptus
No doctrinal point is built on the disputed verses without the dispute being noted
The passage is still treated pastorally and exegetically, not merely dismissed
SDABC and Adventist scholarship on the long ending are consulted or honestly flagged as unread
Verification Ledger present, with the textual-critical claims tagged appropriately

The HTML carries the same content and citations but no Verification Ledger, no para_id, no HTTP codes, no tier markers, and no bare URLs as link text. expectations: Both bible-study.md and bible-study.html are produced and saved in the same dated output folder

Every section is wrapped in <section class="sec" data-hue="N"> with a numbered badge
Scripture uses blockquote.scripture and EGW uses blockquote.egw
Every table is wrapped in div.tablewrap
Numbered lists use one <ol> and count 1..n rather than restarting at 1
